To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spin in abstracts was found in 46.7% of the RCTs analysed.
spin was present in 46.7% of abstracts of randomized controlled trial (n = 45) published in the top 7 obesity and 4 general medicine journals from 2016 and2017.

21 of 45 (46%) of the obesity medicine randomized controlled trial abstracts published in 2015 and 2016 had spin, and 6 (15%) of 39 randomized controlled trials that reported clinical trial registry had evidence of selective outcome reporting bias.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential influence of spin in abstracts of RCTs published by top‐ranked medical journals in the field of obesity medicine.
the presence of selective outcome reporting bias in abstracts of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) published in top‐ranking obesity and general medical journals.
the potential for bias in the abstracts of randomized trials in the field of obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are frequent examples of spin in abstracts of obesity RCTs published from top‐rank journals in 2016‐2017.
spin is common in abstracts of obesity medicine RCT.
there is evidence that spin is present within abstracts of obesity RCTs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the authors found spin to be prevalent in the abstracts of randomized controlled trials in obesity medicine, but that the prevalence of spin may be less in general medicine.
there is a need for more transparency in reporting of results of clinical trials in the abstract.
spin is common in abstracts from RCTs with non‐significant results, but is less prevalent in RCTs that are adequately registered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spin is present in the abstracts of RCTs with non‐significant results.
spin may exist and should be evaluated in the future.
spin may be a problem in RCT abstracts and may influence readers' perception of the trial results, which in turn may influence their clinical practice.
